{{Short description|Canadian scientist}}
'''Martin Alexander Ernst '''"'''Marty'''"''' Bergmann''' (19 February 1956 – 20 August 2011)<ref name=ottcit>{{Cite news|title= Martin Bergmann, Obituary |date= 27 August 2011 |url= http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/ottawacitizen/obituary.aspx?pid=153300016 |newspaper= [[Ottawa Citizen]] |publisher= Postmedia |access-date= 14 November 2016 }}</ref><ref name=grebmier>{{Cite book|title= The Pacific Arctic Region: Ecosystem Status and Trends in a Rapidly Changing Environment |editor1= Grebmeier, J.M. |editor-link=Jacqueline M. Grebmeier|editor2= Maslowski, W. |year= 2014 |publisher= Springer |isbn= 978-94-017-8862-5 }}</ref> was a Canadian scientist and public servant. A marine biologist by training, Bergmann spent 24 years with the Canadian federal Department of Fisheries and Oceans, latterly as Director of the Centre of Expertise for Arctic Aquatic Research Excellence, before taking up the position of head of [[Natural Resources Canada]]'s [[Polar Continental Shelf Program]]. During his career in the [[Public Service of Canada]] Bergmann was instrumental in greatly expanding Canada's Arctic research capabilities. He was a leading player in establishing the [[International Polar Year]] of 2007–2008, and has been called a "leading and relentless evangelist in national and international scientific circles" by the [[Royal Canadian Geographical Society]] (RCGS).<ref name=rcgs2012>{{Cite web |title= The Martin Bergmann Medal for Excellence in Arctic Leadership and Science: 2012 Recipient - Martin "Marty" Bergmann |url= http://www.rcgs.org/awards/bergmann_medal/winner_bergmann2012.asp |website= RCGS.org |publisher= The Royal Canadian Geographical Society |access-date= 14 November 2016 |archive-date= 12 July 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170712022724/http://www.rcgs.org/awards/bergmann_medal/winner_bergmann2012.asp |url-status= dead }}</ref> He died in the crash of [[First Air Flight 6560]] near [[Resolute, Nunavut]], on 20 August 2011. Since his death numerous memorials have been made to Bergmann, including the naming of the [[Arctic Research Foundation]] research vessel ''Martin Bergmann'',<ref name=arctic>{{Cite journal|title= Martin Alexander Bergman (1956–2011) |url= http://pubs.aina.ucalgary.ca/arctic/Arctic65-1-113.pdf |author= Struzik, E. |date= March 2012 |journal= Arctic |volume= 65 |issue= 1 |pages= 113–114 |doi=10.14430/arctic4178}}</ref> the establishment of the RCGS's ''Martin Bergmann Medal'', and the naming of a 375 million year-old fossil fish species found in Nunavut, ''[[Holoptychius|Holoptychius bergmanni]]'', in recognition of his "scientific endeavors [that] communicated the relevance of the Arctic region to a global audience."<ref name=kokan>{{Cite web|title= Predatory ancient fish named after Canadian Arctic scientist Martin Bergmann |url= http://www.janekokan.com/ancient-fish-name-after-canadian-scientist/ |author= Kokan, J. |website= JaneKokan.com |date= 15 April 2013 |access-date= 14 November 2016 }}</ref><ref name=downsetal>{{Cite journal|title= ''Holoptychius bergmanni'' sp. nov. (Sarcopterygii, Porolepiformes) from the Upper Devonian of Nunavut, Canada, and a review of ''Holoptychius'' taxonomy |author1= Downs, J.P. |author2= Daeschler, E.B. |author3= Jenkins Jr., F.A. |author4= Shubin, N.H. |year= 2013 |url= http://www.bioone.org/doi/abs/10.1635/053.162.0104 |journal= Proceedings of the Academy of Natural Sciences of Philadelphia |volume= 162 |issue= 1 |pages= 47–59 |doi=10.1635/053.162.0104|s2cid= 129457144 |url-access= subscription }}</ref>
